text:
people_ops_anna: Thanks for staying after the all-hands pricing section — leadership said they'd hang here for quick Qs about rate limits, packaging, credits, and quotas. Drop short items.

eng_jules: If multiple services share a project key, will a noisy service starve others?

cto_jen: Yes — project keys share project-level quotas. Recommended: one project per environment/service or enable org-level quotas for cross-team governance.

eng_jules: Is there an endpoint to check remaining tokens so CI can gate runs?

infra_ryan: Yep. Example curl to poll remaining tokens for a project:

```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/usage/projects/PROJECT_ID/remaining
```

product_maya: We're adding a small SDK helper for polling + backoff to the docs this week.

eng_jules: What codes do we expect so CI can handle them properly?

cto_jen: 429 = rate-limit window exceeded (Retry-After header included). 402 = hard spend cap / payment-block event. Use conservative retry for 429s, fail fast on 402.

finance_kim: Trial credits expire 90 days after issuance. Promo credit expirations are shown at redemption and in Billing -> Credits.

eng_jules: If a project is flagged for abuse, will other projects in the same org be affected?

cto_jen: Typically we isolate to the offending project. In escalated incidents we may apply org-level mitigations while investigating and will notify account contacts.

people_ops_anna: Are hard spend caps configurable per project? We want CI to never spend beyond budget.

product_maya: Yes 1 Console -> Billing supports soft alerts and hard caps per project. Soft = alerts, Hard = block (returns 402). Enterprise can request account-wide spend controls.

eng_jules: Do embeddings have distinct quotas? We run continuous vector jobs.

cto_jen: Embeddings are metered separately (vector units/min) and have their own concurrency safeguards. Batch 32128 vectors and use the batch embeddings API to stay efficient.

infra_ryan: We hit a burst last week 5 any automatic downgrade to a smaller model?

cto_jen: No silent downgrades. Default is a hard 429. You can opt into route-level failover to a cheaper/compatible variant via routing policies. That behavior must be configured per route.

eng_jules: Retry guidance?

product_maya: Use exponential backoff + jitter and respect Retry-After. SDKs include retry helpers; background jobs can opt into slower aggressive retry configs.

billing_bot: [billing] Reminder: expiring credits show a banner on Console home and under Billing -> Credits. For special credit handling contact billing@redwood.ai.

people_ops_anna: Product will publish a concise FAQ + examples (per-route quotas, curl/SDK snippets, spend caps, org quotas) tomorrow and we'll pin it here. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
